reports.title: Karen O'Brien
categories: Hospital Death (Clinical Procedures and medical management) related deaths

concerns.quote: It is difficult to understand how there can be a clinical determination by SEPT without more inquiry and, preferably, some face-to-face assessment of the patient by a mental health professional.
The NICE guidance is stated to be a recommendation. It must therefore be presumed not to be applied slavishly without careful assessment.
On what basis did SEPT decide to override the GP's request?
I respectfully invite NICE to reconsider the guideline.

links.explanation: Both reports highlight that clinicians are applying NICE guidance too rigidly, leading to inadequate patient assessment. The earlier case concerns missed head injury due to lack of neurological signs; the later case concerns overriding a GP request without proper evaluation.
links.earlier_quote: The Emergency Department doctors indicated that they could not get a CT of the head because "the NICE Guidelines do not indicate as being appropriate where there are no obvious neurological signs".
links.later_quote: The NICE guidance is stated to be a recommendation. It must therefore be presumed not to be applied slavishly without careful assessment.
